newsitem.title: UK: Britain's top financial regulator to stand down.
newsitem.headline: Britain's top financial regulator to stand down.

text.p: The chairman of Britain's Securities and Investments Board, Sir Andrew Large, will stand down and not seek to renew his five year term of office, the SIB said on Thursday.
"I feel after five years that it is right to move on," Large, the longest serving head of Britain's top financial regulatory body, said in a statement.
"The main unfinished piece of business is the unsatisfactory rate of progress on the pensions review. This will be a key focal point for me in my remaining period of office."
"I was charged to oversee the implementation of evolutionary change outlined in my 1993 review. The bulk of this is now complete. So this is the logical time for a change of chairman," said Large.

Large is accredited with unscrambling the complex web of self-regulatory bodies, inherited from the 1986 Financial Services Act, which he cut down to three with the SIB as its overlord. He also pressed through the establishment of the Personal Investment Authority despite stern opposition from the Prudential, Britain's largest insurance company.

Large, formerly a main board director at Swiss Bank Corp, also tightened regulation of Britain's markets like the London Metal Exchange and improved co-operation overseas with other regulators in the wake of the collapses of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International and Barings.
"In addition, I will be handing on to my successor an effective executive team and a well developed work programme for addressing newer issues which have developed," said Large.
